intro: Continents, weather on the road and people who move to a new city.
p.continente.consejo: Europe, Asia and Africa are continents.
p.océano.consejo: It has an accent on the é: «o-THE-a-no». The Atlantic and the Pacific are oceans.
p.península.consejo: It has an accent on the í: «pe-NIN-su-la». Spain and Portugal are on the Iberian peninsula.
p.población.consejo: It comes from «poblar». «La población de una ciudad» is all its inhabitants.
p.turista.consejo: It works for a man and a woman: «el turista», «la turista».
p.viajero.consejo: For a woman: «la viajera». The v sounds b and the j sounds h: «bya-HE-ro».
p.mudarse.consejo: It takes «se»: «me mudo, te mudas». It is used with «a»: «me mudé a Madrid».
p.maleta.consejo: It is feminine: «la maleta». To pack it you say «hacer la maleta».
p.tormenta.consejo: In a storm you see the lightning first and hear the thunder afterwards.
p.niebla.consejo: You say «hay niebla» when you can see little. In English, «fog».
p.ola de calor.consejo: It is not a wave of the sea. Do not confuse it with «hola», which has an h.
p.barrio.consejo: The «rr» is strong: «BA-rryo». A big city has many neighbourhoods.
p.echar de menos.consejo: You also say «extrañar», especially in Latin America.
b1.texto:
In the world there are **continentes** and **océanos**. A **península** is land surrounded by water on almost all sides.

When you travel, the weather can change: a **tormenta**, **niebla** or an **ola de calor**.

A **turista** or a **viajero** visits a place and goes home. Whoever **se muda** changes house and **barrio**, with their **maleta**. You can **echar de menos** the people and your home city.

The **población** of a city is the people who live in it.
b2.f1.texto: I am from a small city, near the ocean.
b2.f2.texto: Why did you move to this city?
b2.f3.texto: I moved to study and I found a good job.
b2.f5.texto: I miss the food and my family.
b2.f6.texto: Adapting to another city is not easy.
b2.f7.texto: Each new neighbourhood teaches me something different.
b4.titulo: Telling a trip: simple past and imperfect
b4.texto:
To tell a trip, use two pasts:

- **Indefinido**: what happened, a finished action: **hubo una tormenta**, **llegamos al puerto**.
- **Imperfecto**: what the situation was like or what happened often: **hacía mucho calor**, **había niebla**.

They combine: **cuando llegamos, hacía frío**.

With **haber**: the simple past is **hubo** and the imperfect is **había**. **Hay** becomes **hubo** for an event, and **había** when describing.
b4.e0.texto: Yesterday there was a storm on the coast.
b4.e1.texto: It was very hot in the city.
b4.e2.texto: When we arrived, there was fog.
b5.f0.texto: The train leaves the station as dawn breaks over the wet roofs.
b5.f1.texto: Amal holds an old suitcase between her knees and looks out of the window.
b5.f2.texto: A thick fog covers the valley like a woollen blanket.
b5.f3.texto: Among the clouds a ray of sun suddenly appears over the river.
b5.f4.texto: The travellers doze with their heads resting on the cold glass.
b5.f5.texto: At midday the train reaches a city of wide streets.
b5.f6.texto: Amal gets off with her suitcase and breathes a different air.
b5.f7.texto: On the platform, an old man sells oranges under a blue umbrella.
b5.f8.texto: The new neighbourhood smells of freshly baked bread and rain.
b5.f9.texto: Amal misses the sea of her hometown and smiles slowly.
b6.o0.refuerzo: Well done! «Hubo» is the simple past of «haber» for an event.
b6.o1.refuerzo: «Fue» comes from «ser» or «ir». For «there was» you use «hubo».
b6.o2.refuerzo: «Tuvo» comes from «tener». For «there was» you use «hubo».
b6.pregunta: Yesterday something happened in the sky. What is missing?
b7.o0.refuerzo: If you go on holiday, you return to your home.
b7.o1.refuerzo: Packing a suitcase is just a part of the trip.
b7.o2.refuerzo: That's it! You go to live somewhere else.
b8.frase: Amal echa de menos su ciudad natal
b9.o0: una ola grande en el mar
b9.o0.refuerzo: It is another «ola»: here we are not talking about the sea.
b9.o1: un periodo de temperaturas muy altas
b9.o1.refuerzo: Yes! It is several days in a row of great heat.
b9.o2.refuerzo: The greeting is «hola», with an h. There is no greeting here.
b9.pregunta: What does «una ola de calor» mean?
b10.o0.refuerzo: «Hizo» tells an event; to describe you use the imperfect.
b10.o1.refuerzo: «Hace» is present, but the sentence is about the past.
b10.o2.refuerzo: Correct! The imperfect describes what the weather was like.
b10.pregunta: You describe what the weather was like. What is missing?
b12.o0.refuerzo: That's it! The Atlantic is an ocean.
b12.o1.refuerzo: The Mediterranean is a sea, smaller than an ocean.
b12.o2.refuerzo: The Amazon is a river, not an ocean.
b12.pregunta: Which of these is an ocean?
p.mudaste.consejo: From «mudarse», to move house. The ending «-aste» is the past for «tú». Stress falls on «DAS».
p.mudé.consejo: From «mudarse». The accent on the final «é» marks the past for «yo». Stress falls on the last syllable.
p.echas.consejo: From «echar de menos», to miss someone. «Echas» is the form for «tú». Stress is on «E».
p.natal.consejo: Used with «ciudad» to mean the city where you were born. The stress falls on «TAL».
p.adaptarse.glosa: to adapt, to get used to
p.adaptarse.consejo: From «adaptar», to adjust. The «-se» at the end means you adapt yourself.
p.diferente.consejo: It stays the same for masculine and feminine: «un barrio diferente», «una ciudad diferente».
p.llegamos.consejo: From «llegar», to arrive. The «ll» sounds like «y» here, and the stress falls on «GA».
p.amanece.consejo: From «amanecer», to dawn. In Spain the «c» before «e» sounds like «th».
p.dormitan.consejo: From «dormitar», to doze. It means sleeping lightly, like a short nap.
p.apoyada.consejo: Feminine form of «apoyado». It agrees with «cabeza», which is feminine.
p.anchas.consejo: Feminine plural of «ancho», wide. It agrees with «calles», which are feminine.
p.vende.consejo: From «vender», to sell. The «v» sounds like «b» in Spanish.
p.periodo.consejo: Often written «período» with an accent. Here it means a stretch of time, like some weeks.
p.temperaturas.consejo: The stress falls on «TU». It is plural, so it means several readings of heat or cold.
